29/// A specific tag which allows accessing attributes specific to this [`TagKind`].
30///
31/// # Example
32/// ```
33/// use std::num::NonZeroU32;
34/// use krilla::tagging::{TagGroup, TagTree, TableHeaderScope, Tag, TagId};
35///
36/// let tag = Tag::TH(TableHeaderScope::Row)
37///     .with_id(Some(TagId::from(*b"this id")))
38///     .with_col_span(Some(NonZeroU32::new(3).unwrap()))
39///     .with_headers(Some([TagId::from(*b"parent id")]))
40///     .with_width(Some(250.0))
41///     .with_height(Some(100.0));
42/// let group = TagGroup::new(tag);
43///
44/// let mut tree = TagTree::new();
45/// tree.push(group);
46/// ```
47#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
48pub struct Tag<T> {
49    inner: AnyTag,
50    /// Compile time marker for a type-safe API.
51    pub(crate) ty: PhantomData<T>,
52}
53
54impl<T> Tag<T> {
55    /// This can't be public, otherwise tags could be constructed without
56    /// providing required attributes.
57    pub(crate) const fn new() -> Self {
58        Self {
59            inner: AnyTag::new(),
60            ty: PhantomData,
61        }
62    }
63
64    /// A raw tag, which allows reading all attributes.
65    pub fn as_any(&self) -> &AnyTag {
66        &self.inner
67    }
68
69    /// A raw tag, which allows reading all attributes and additionally writing
70    /// all global ones.
71    pub fn as_any_mut(&mut self) -> &mut AnyTag {
72        &mut self.inner
73    }
74
75    /// Get the location.
76    pub fn location(&self) -> Option<Location> {
77        self.as_any().location
78    }
79
80    /// Set the location.
81    pub fn set_location(&mut self, location: Option<Location>) {
82        self.as_any_mut().location = location;
83    }
84
85    /// Set the location.
86    pub fn with_location(mut self, location: Option<Location>) -> Self {
87        self.as_any_mut().location = location;
88        self
89    }
90}

110/// An ordered set using ordinal numbers to sort and identify elements.
111#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
112pub(crate) struct OrdinalSet<A> {
113    items: SmallVec<[A; 1]>,
114}
115
116impl<A> OrdinalSet<A> {
117    pub(crate) const fn new() -> Self {
118        Self {
119            items: SmallVec::new_const(),
120        }
121    }
122}
123
124impl<A: Ordinal> OrdinalSet<A> {
125    pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &A> {
126        self.items.iter()
127    }
128
129    pub(crate) fn set(&mut self, attr: A) {
130        for (i, item) in self.items.iter().enumerate() {
131            if item.ordinal() == attr.ordinal() {
132                self.items[i] = attr;
133                return;
134            }
135            if item.ordinal() > attr.ordinal() {
136                self.items.insert(i, attr);
137                return;
138            }
139        }
140        self.items.push(attr);
141    }
142
143    pub(crate) fn remove(&mut self, ordinal: usize) {
144        for (i, item) in self.items.iter().enumerate() {
145            if item.ordinal() == ordinal {
146                self.items.remove(i);
147                return;
148            }
149            if item.ordinal() > ordinal {
150                break;
151            }
152        }
153    }
154
155    pub(crate) fn get(&self, ordinal: usize) -> Option<&A> {
156        for item in self.items.iter() {
157            if item.ordinal() == ordinal {
158                return Some(item);
159            }
160            if item.ordinal() > ordinal {
161                break;
162            }
163        }
164        None
165    }
166
167    pub(crate) fn set_or_remove(&mut self, ordinal: usize, attr: Option<A>) {
168        match attr {
169            Some(attr) => self.set(attr),
170            None => self.remove(ordinal),
171        }
172    }
173}
174
175/// Identifies elements using an ordinal number.
176pub(crate) trait Ordinal {
177    fn ordinal(&self) -> usize;
178}

184impl<I: IntoIterator<Item = u8>> From<I> for TagId {
185    fn from(value: I) -> Self {
186        // Disambiguate ids provided by the user from ids automatically assigned
187        // to notes by prefixing them with a `U`.
188        let bytes = std::iter::once(b'U').chain(value).collect();
189        TagId(bytes)
190    }
191}

195    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
196        self.0.as_slice()

260/// The positioning of the element with respect to the enclosing reference area
261/// and other content.
262/// When applied to an ILSE, any value except Inline shall cause the element to
263/// be treated as a BLSE instead.
264///
265/// Default value: [`Placement::Inline`].
266#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
267pub enum Placement {
268    /// Stacked in the block-progression direction within an enclosing reference
269    /// area or parent BLSE.
270    Block,
271    /// Packed in the inline-progression direction within an enclosing BLSE.
272    #[default]
273    Inline,
274    /// Placed so that the before edge of the element’s allocation rectangle.
275    /// (see “Content and Allocation Rectangles” in 14.8.5.4, “Layout Attributes”)
276    /// coincides with that of the nearest enclosing reference area. The element
277    /// may float, if necessary, to achieve the specified placement. The element
278    /// shall be treated as a block occupying the full extent of the enclosing
279    /// reference area in the inline direction. Other content shall be stacked
280    /// so as to begin at the after edge of the element’s allocation rectangle.
281    Before,
282    /// Placed so that the start edge of the element’s allocation rectangle
283    /// (see “Content and Allocation Rectangles” in 14.8.5.4, “Layout Attributes”)
284    /// coincides with that of the nearest enclosing reference area. The element
285    /// may float, if necessary, to achieve the specified placement. Other
286    /// content that would intrude into the element’s allocation rectangle
287    /// shall be laid out as a runaround.
288    Start,
289    /// Placed so that the end edge of the element’s allocation rectangle
290    /// (see “Content and Allocation Rectangles” in 14.8.5.4, “Layout Attributes”)
291    /// coincides with that of the nearest enclosing reference area. The element
292    /// may float, if necessary, to achieve the specified placement. Other
293    /// content that would intrude into the element’s allocation rectangle
294    /// shall be laid out as a runaround.
295    End,
296}
297
298impl Placement {
299    pub(crate) fn to_pdf(self) -> pdf_writer::types::Placement {
300        match self {
301            Placement::Block => pdf_writer::types::Placement::Block,
302            Placement::Inline => pdf_writer::types::Placement::Inline,
303            Placement::Before => pdf_writer::types::Placement::Before,
304            Placement::Start => pdf_writer::types::Placement::Start,
305            Placement::End => pdf_writer::types::Placement::End,
306        }
307    }
308}

310/// The directions of layout progression for packing of ILSEs (inline progression)
311/// and stacking of BLSEs (block progression).
312/// The specified layout directions shall apply to the given structure element
313/// and all of its descendants to any level of nesting.
314///
315/// Default value: [`WritingMode::LrTb`].
316#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
317pub enum WritingMode {
318    /// Inline progression from left to right; block progression from top to
319    /// bottom. This is the typical writing mode for Western writing systems.
320    #[default]
321    LrTb,
322    /// Inline progression from right to left; block progression from top to
323    /// bottom. This is the typical writing mode for Arabic and Hebrew writing
324    /// systems.
325    RlTb,
326    /// Inline progression from top to bottom; block progression from right to
327    /// left. This is the typical writing mode for Chinese and Japanese writing
328    /// systems.
329    TbRl,
330}
331
332impl WritingMode {
333    pub(crate) fn to_pdf(self) -> pdf_writer::types::WritingMode {
334        match self {
335            WritingMode::LrTb => pdf_writer::types::WritingMode::LtrTtb,
336            WritingMode::RlTb => pdf_writer::types::WritingMode::RtlTtb,
337            WritingMode::TbRl => pdf_writer::types::WritingMode::TtbRtl,
338        }
339    }
340}

359/// An RGB color within the tag tree. The color space of this color is not
360/// specified. Each component is in the range [0.0, 1.0].
361#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
362pub struct NaiveRgbColor {
363    /// The red component of the color.
364    pub red: u8,
365    /// The green component of the color.
366    pub green: u8,
367    /// The blue component of the color.
368    pub blue: u8,
369}
370
371impl NaiveRgbColor {
372    /// Create a new RGB color.
373    pub fn new(red: u8, green: u8, blue: u8) -> Self {
374        Self { red, green, blue }
375    }
376
377    /// Create a new RGB color from normalized floating point values.
378    pub fn new_f32(red: f32, green: f32, blue: f32) -> Self {
379        if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&red)
380            || !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&green)
381            || !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&blue)
382        {
383            panic!("RGB color components must be in the range [0.0, 1.0]");
384        }
385        Self {
386            red: (255.0 * red).round() as u8,
387            green: (255.0 * green).round() as u8,
388            blue: (255.0 * blue).round() as u8,
389        }
390    }
391
392    /// Convert the color into an array of f32 components for PDF serialization.
393    pub fn into_f32_array(self) -> [f32; 3] {
394        let normalize = |n| n as f32 / 255.0;
395        [self.red, self.green, self.blue].map(normalize)
396    }
397}
398
399impl From<NaiveRgbColor> for crate::graphics::color::rgb::Color {
400    fn from(color: NaiveRgbColor) -> Self {
401        crate::graphics::color::rgb::Color::new(color.red, color.green, color.blue)
402    }
403}
404
405impl From<NaiveRgbColor> for [f32; 3] {
406    fn from(color: NaiveRgbColor) -> Self {
407        color.into_f32_array()
408    }
409}

568/// The rotation of glyphs in vertical writing modes.
569#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
570pub enum GlyphOrientationVertical {
571    /// Determine the rotation based on whether the text is full-width.
572    Auto,
573    /// No rotation.
574    None,
575    /// Rotate 90 degrees clockwise.
576    Clockwise90,
577    /// Rotate 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
578    CounterClockwise90,
579    /// Rotate 180 degrees clockwise.
580    Clockwise180,
581    /// Rotate 180 degrees counter-clockwise.
582    CounterClockwise180,
583    /// Rotate 270 degrees clockwise.
584    Clockwise270,
585}
586
587impl GlyphOrientationVertical {
588    /// Convert the rotation to a number. If the rotation is `Auto`, returns
589    /// `None`.
590    pub(super) fn to_pdf(self) -> pdf_writer::types::GlyphOrientationVertical {
591        let angle = match self {
592            GlyphOrientationVertical::Auto => {
593                return pdf_writer::types::GlyphOrientationVertical::Auto
594            }
595            GlyphOrientationVertical::None => 0,
596            GlyphOrientationVertical::Clockwise90 => 90,
597            GlyphOrientationVertical::CounterClockwise90 => -90,
598            GlyphOrientationVertical::Clockwise180 => 180,
599            GlyphOrientationVertical::CounterClockwise180 => -180,
600            GlyphOrientationVertical::Clockwise270 => 270,
601        };
602        pdf_writer::types::GlyphOrientationVertical::Angle(angle)
603    }
604}

606/// An attribute value that can apply to all sides of the element, or have a specific value for each side.
607#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
608pub struct Sides<T> {
609    /// The start of the element on the block axis.
610    pub before: T,
611    /// The end of the element on the block axis.
612    pub after: T,
613    /// The start of the element on the inline axis.
614    pub start: T,
615    /// The end of the element on the inline axis.
616    pub end: T,
617}
618
619impl<T> Sides<T> {
620    /// Construct a new `Sides` value with specific values for each side.
621    pub fn new(before: T, after: T, start: T, end: T) -> Self {
622        Self {
623            before,
624            after,
625            start,
626            end,
627        }
628    }
629
630    /// Construct a new `Sides` value with the same value for all sides.
631    pub fn uniform(value: T) -> Self
632    where
633        T: Copy,
634    {
635        Sides {
636            before: value,
637            after: value,
638            start: value,
639            end: value,
640        }
641    }
642
643    pub(crate) fn is_uniform(&self) -> bool
644    where
645        T: PartialEq,
646    {
647        self.before == self.after && self.before == self.start && self.before == self.end
648    }
649
650    /// Returns an array for all sides.
651    pub(super) fn into_array(self) -> [T; 4] {
652        [self.before, self.after, self.start, self.end]
653    }
654
655    /// Convert into [`pdf_writer::types::Sides`].
656    pub(super) fn into_pdf(self) -> pdf_writer::types::Sides<T> {
657        pdf_writer::types::Sides::from_array(self.into_array())
658    }
659
660    /// Convert into [`pdf_writer::types::Sides`] by each side value.
661    pub(super) fn map_pdf<P>(self, to_pdf: impl Fn(T) -> P) -> pdf_writer::types::Sides<P> {
662        pdf_writer::types::Sides::from_array(self.into_array().map(to_pdf))
663    }
664}
